states_condition_for_every_entry.instructions: Does `comment.text` state at least one condition that every entry of the list in `code.after_comment` must meet?

true.what: `comment.text` says that all entries of the shown list share at least one property, or that the list holds only entries of one kind, such as 'only read-only methods' or 'every timeout is in seconds'.
true.not_for: A statement about the list as a whole (its length, its order, where it is used) and statements about code other than the shown list.
examples: `# Only idempotent HTTP methods, so a retry is always safe.` above `SAFE = ("GET", "HEAD", "PUT")`

false.what: `comment.text` states no condition that each entry must meet.
examples: `# Checked in this order; the first match wins.` above a list of patterns

entry_meets_stated_condition.instructions: Does the entry in `{item}.code` meet every condition that `comment.text` states for all entries of the list?

true.what: Read as written, each condition in `comment.text` is true of the entry in `{item}.code`, with the code in `{item}.definitions` when the entry names other code.
true.not_for: Whether the conditions are a good rule, and whether the entry is useful.
examples: The comment says 'only read-only methods' and the entry is `"GET"`.
The comment says 'every timeout is in seconds' and the entry is `RETRY_TIMEOUT = 30`.

false.what: Read as written, the entry in `{item}.code` fails at least one condition that `comment.text` states for all entries.
examples: The comment says 'only read-only methods' and the entry is `"POST"`.
The comment says 'every pattern matches a file name, never a folder' and the entry is `re.compile(r"(^|/)build/")`.
